current_answer: People have built games, browser demos, desktop apps, art, brain engines and research tests on real fruit fly connectomes, mainly FlyWire (female brain) and MaleCNS (male brain and nerve cord). We checked 82 of them on 29 September 2026: 31 can be opened in a browser or free notebook without installing anything. Most viral demos really run a simulated fly brain, but a person chose which neurons receive the input and which neurons act, and several get most of their movement from scripts or trained parts; the Half-Life demo does not load a connectome at all by default, and DesktopFly (re-graded to C) mostly switches coded animations. No fly has been "uploaded". This week's two viral claims publish no code: the Raspberry Pi "fly plays Pokémon" stream may run a full FlyWire brain, but its input is read from game memory, its decoder is unpublished and chat steers learning, so it cannot show what the fly contributes; the "fly plays Rainbow Six Siege" claim of over 1,000,000 neurons matches no fly connectome. Where studies use shuffled-wiring controls, the real wiring matters for fly reflexes and for steering a simulated body (a new closed-loop study: 2.96 poles per 10 s with real wiring vs 0.34 scrambled), but it has not helped general machine-learning tasks, and in Doom a brainless constant autopilot survives about as long as the viral full-brain fly (51.9 s vs 53.3 s). A beginner can run the published whole-brain model on a CPU: in our test on 2 CPUs (Linux, 28 minutes) sugar input drove the feeding motor neuron to 85.2 Hz, and shuffled wiring dropped it to 0 Hz.

catalogue_card.question: What have people built with the digital fruit fly brain, and what is real?
catalogue_card.text: 82 fruit fly brain simulation projects checked in code: 31 you can try online, 47 demo and lab videos with evidence grades, verdicts on 16 viral claims and wiring tests for Doom and a walking fly.

summary: 82 entries checked on 29 Sep 2026 (9 new in the third check): 18 grade A, 12 B, 20 C, 3 D, 7 U and 22 datasets or tools (not graded).

Pokémon on a Raspberry Pi 5 (Twitch, XDA Developers, 28 Sep 2026): grade U. A full FlyWire brain may well run on the Pi, but by the creator's own account the brain reads positions from game memory, the button decoder and helper scripts are unpublished and chat steers learning, so the stream cannot show how much of the progress comes from the fly. Two open-source Pokémon fly projects (acamilo/flybrain and fly-plays-games, both grade C) are not the stream's code, judging by mismatches rather than proof.

Rainbow Six Siege fly brain (dev.ua, 28 Sep 2026): grade U. Nothing is published; the stated "over 1,000,000 neurons" matches no fly connectome (MaleCNS v1.0 166,700; FlyWire v783 139,255), and training on 20 TB of human gameplay would explain any skill.

DesktopFly re-graded from B to C on 29 Sep 2026 (code unchanged): neuron rates only switch coded flight, grooming and dart animations, sleep follows the computer's idle time and clock, and only walking is driven by simulated leg neurons. There is no official app download; copies under other accounts that ship a zip with a Windows program are download lures.

Wiring test (fly-brain-zero-shot, grade A): an eye model, the whole FlyWire brain and a NeuroMechFly body reach 2.96 poles per 10 s with real wiring, 0.34 with scrambled wiring and 0.12 with turn neurons disconnected (3.14, 0.12 and 0.52 after two legs are cut; authors' numbers, means recomputed by us). Walking comes from a hand-built rhythm; the brain only steers.

Doom: in a third-party control study using DOOMFLY's own code, a brainless constant autopilot survived 51.9 s against 53.3 s for the full MaleCNS brain; shuffled wiring 6.7 s. The autopilot copies the fly's average output, so a constant policy reproduces the behaviour; this does not show the brain does nothing. DOOMFLY stays grade B.
31 entries have a no-install link (one is a live stream); all answered our HTTP check, but none was played by us.

In viral demos a real connectome usually runs, but people chose the input and output neurons; DesktopFly, FlyCraft, Bad Apple, FlyDrones, the FlyBridge Minecraft farming demo and the Roblox maze race get much of their visible behaviour from scripts, stimulus, training or a synthetic network, and the Half-Life demo (grade D) builds a synthetic network by default although its videos claim MaleCNS v1.0 and "no scripted game AI".
Beat Saber, NeuroCraft, Eon's embodied fly, the Pokémon stream and the Rainbow Six claim have no inspectable code (grade U).

Video gallery (29 Sep 2026): 47 videos, 42 of them original uploads by the project's author, lab or institution; 29 of 82 catalogue entries have at least one video. Each card shows the project's grade from the catalogue and what the video does not show.
The most-watched demo clips are the least checkable: Beat Saber (about 23 million views) and NeuroCraft are grade U, and Bad Apple is grade C because its picture is mostly the stimulus.
"91%" is the share of 164 testable predictions of the brain-only Shiu et al. 2024 model that matched experiments; "95%" compares versions of the model and is not an accuracy.

Controlled studies (20): shuffled wiring abolishes fly reflexes (for example MN9 0 Hz vs 67.30 Hz) and stops a simulated fly steering to targets, but fly wiring did no better than random or shuffled wiring on reservoir, language-model, hashing and trained Doom tasks (authors' numbers).
FlyWire data is CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); MaleCNS, MANC, hemibrain and BANC data are CC BY.

Build your own, tested 28 Sep 2026 on Linux with 2 CPUs and no GPU: the Shiu et al. model on FlyWire v783 gave MN9 85.2 ± 3.2 Hz with sugar input at 150 Hz, 0 Hz without input, and 0 Hz in 6 of 6 trials with shuffled wiring; 6 of 6 tests passed. Project pages cover the Shiu et al. model, DOOMFLY and DesktopFly.
uncertainty: No demo was played in a real browser; "page responds" is an HTTP check only. No project was built or run in the 29 Sep 2026 check.

Control and benchmark numbers are the authors' own (a third party's for doom-fly-control); we re-computed only two statistics from published files (larva vs shuffles; the fly-brain-zero-shot means). Several controls are small: one training seed, 4 runs per shuffle seed, 2 races, 16 flies from one shuffle.

Borderline grades: Fly Worker, fly-brain by Lulzx, The Fly's Hash Function, Fly OCR, Fly Self Driving (headline numbers only in its results document; stored JSON does not match), the null-model study (brain compressed to 512 groups) and fly-brain-zero-shot (hand-built walking rhythm, one tuned steering gain) are borderline A; fly-brain by erojas and Kick the Fly could argue B; acamilo-flybrain would sit on the B/C border without its stream macros.

The five C grades added on 28 Sep 2026 and the fafbseg entry rest on file citations that we spot-read but did not re-verify line by line. fly-plays-games runs its neurons in an external package (fly.ai) that we did not inspect.

The Pokémon stream and the Rainbow Six claim are known only through news articles, a Reddit post and a Twitch page read through summarising tools or search summaries; dev.ua blocks our fetches, and X, TikTok and Reddit cannot be searched without a login. "Not the stream's code" rests on mismatches, not proof.
Stars, creation and last-push dates of 56 records were reused from our 27 or 28 Sep 2026 checks and are labelled with those dates.
Why the Shiu v783 file has 616 fewer neurons than the FlyWire v783 release is not established; the scope of BANC's "approximately 188,000 neurons" is not stated.
The Beat Saber explanation and the MICrONS figures rest on search summaries only.

Not yet triaged: two graded entries held back (flykart, making-fly-play-chess), about 211 repositories listed only in project directories, 13 new Fly Brain Hub leads and other low-star GitHub leads. X and TikTok were not searched for new videos.
The Build your own guide is untested on macOS, Windows/WSL, Colab and machines with a C++ compiler; GitHub Pages publishing is untested. DOOMFLY's and DesktopFly's run steps are untested by us.
FlyWire data licence conflict: CC BY-NC 4.0 in the official guidelines vs CC BY 4.0 on the Zenodo v783 record; we follow the stricter, non-commercial reading.

Video summaries rest on titles, descriptions, captions, code and thumbnails; we did not watch every video frame by frame. View counts are snapshots from 28 Sep 2026 (29 Sep for the newest video). The Half-Life video's uploader is matched to the code's author by name only.

Videos cannot play inside the site: YouTube, Vimeo, TikTok and X players failed in the site's sandboxed frames (tested in headless Chromium only; Safari, Firefox and mobile untested). YouTube and X thumbnails are loaded from their image servers.
